page.text:
A *matrix* is a two-dimensional rectangular grid of scalars arranged into
rows and columns. Conceived in the nineteenth century by Arthur Cayley
and James Joseph Sylvester, matrices provide the computational machinery
that translates abstract, coordinate-free linear algebra into concrete
numerical algorithms.

When finite-dimensional vector spaces are equipped with ordered bases,
every linear transformation is faithfully encoded by a matrix whose
columns are the coordinate vectors of the basis images. In this
representation, function composition transforms into matrix
multiplication, vector evaluation corresponds to matrix-vector products,
and geometric transformations such as rotations, reflections, and
projections become structured array computations.
